challenges.name: timeouts-rate-limits-evidence
challenges.title: Timeouts, 429s and fallback: read the hint service
challenges.description: Three statements on the CodeDev hint service under load: a per-call timeout without an overall deadline, a 429 with Retry-After, and a call that timed out on our side but not on the provider's.

questions.explanation: False. The timeout limits each attempt, not the request. If the provider hangs, attempt 1 waits 10 s, then 1 s of backoff, attempt 2 another 10 s, 2 s of backoff, attempt 3 another 10 s: about 33 s before the fallback. Long before that the learner has clicked again or left, and the lesson page may have given up on its own. A per-call timeout needs an overall deadline for the whole request: each attempt gets min(per-call timeout, time left), and no retry starts when the deadline would pass during it. The misconception is to read a per-call limit as a limit on what the user waits.

True. The provider said it will not accept another request from us for 20 s; a retry before then is likely to get another 429 and adds to the rate-limit pressure, and a retry after then lands 12 s past the deadline the hint feature promised. The code compares the wait with the time left and degrades at once: the learner gets the fallback (on CodeDev, the static hint of the current level) and can ask again later. The misconception is that honouring Retry-After means always waiting for it; it means not calling before it, and if that does not fit the deadline, not calling at all.

questions.question:
Hint service log:
10:03:17.000 hint req=h_88e1 call=1 timeout after 10000ms (aborted by us)
10:03:18.000 hint req=h_88e1 call=2 status=200 input_tokens=2210 output_tokens=96

Provider usage export for the same minute (request ids from the provider's response headers and from its dashboard):
time       request         status     input_tokens  output_tokens
10:03:07   prov_a91f...    completed          2210            380
10:03:18   prov_b07c...    completed          2210             96

Statement: "Retrying call 1 was free: we aborted it after 10 s, so the provider never finished it and did not count its tokens."
questions.explanation: False. The export shows the first request (started at 10:03:07, the moment call 1 was sent) completed on the provider's side with 380 output tokens, after we had stopped waiting. Aborting stops our client from waiting; it does not reliably stop the work already sent, and the provider's usage, and possibly the bill, can include it. Check your provider's documentation for how cancelled requests are counted. So a retry after a timeout is not free and not idempotent in cost: keep timeouts above the normal slow case, bound the retries, and give each hint request an idempotency key so a double click or a client retry reuses one result instead of calling the model again.
